verses.text: Jerub-Baal—that’s Gideon—and all his people got up early and camped by the Spring of Harod. Midian’s camp was north of them, by Moreh Hill in the valley. 🌅
Yahweh told Gideon, ‘You’ve got too many people for me to hand Midian over to you. Israel might flex against me and say, “I saved myself.”’ 💬
‘So announce this to the people: Anyone scared and shaking can turn back and leave Mount Gilead.’ Twenty-two thousand headed home; ten thousand stayed. 🚶
Yahweh told Gideon, ‘Still too many. Bring them down to the water, and I’ll sort them out there. I’ll tell you who goes with you and who doesn’t.’ 💧
So Gideon brought them to the water. Yahweh told him, ‘Set aside everyone who laps water with their tongue like a dog; do the same with anyone who kneels down to drink.’ 🐕
Three hundred men scooped water up with their hands and lapped it. Everyone else got down on their knees to drink. 🔢
Yahweh told Gideon, ‘I’ll rescue you with these three hundred who lapped, and hand Midian over to you. Send everyone else back home.’ 💪
The people took their food and trumpets. Gideon sent the rest of Israel back to their tents but kept the three hundred. Midian’s camp was down in the valley below him. 🏕️
That same night Yahweh told him, ‘Get up and go down into their camp. I’ve handed it over to you. 🌙
But if you’re scared to go down, take Purah your servant with you. 🤝
Listen to what they’re saying; afterward you’ll have the courage to go into the camp.’ Gideon went down with Purah to the edge of the armed guards. 👂
The Midianites, Amalekites, and all the eastern peoples were spread through the valley like a swarm of locusts. Their camels were beyond counting—like sand by the sea. 🦗
Gideon arrived just as one man was telling his friend a dream: ‘I dreamed a loaf of barley bread tumbled into Midian’s camp, hit a tent, knocked it over, and flattened it.’ 🌙
His friend answered, ‘That can only mean the sword of Gideon son of Joash, an Israelite. God has handed Midian and its whole army over to him.’ 🗡️
When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he bowed in worship. Then he returned to Israel’s camp and said, ‘Get up! Yahweh has handed Midian’s army over to you!’ 🙌
He split the three hundred into three groups and gave each man a trumpet and an empty jar with a torch inside. 🔥
He told them, ‘Watch me and do what I do. When I reach the edge of the camp, copy my moves. 👀
When I blow my trumpet, you all blow yours around the whole camp and shout, “For Yahweh and Gideon!”’ 📯
Gideon and his hundred men reached the camp’s edge at the start of the middle watch, just after the guards had changed. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands. 💥
All three groups blew their trumpets, smashed their jars, held torches in their left hands and trumpets in their right, and shouted, ‘The sword for Yahweh and Gideon!’ 📯
Each man held his spot around the camp. The whole army ran, shouting as they fled. 🏃

As the three hundred trumpets kept sounding, Yahweh turned every Midianite’s sword against his fellow and the whole army. They fled toward Beth Shittah and Zererah, as far as Abel Meholah by Tabbath. ⚔️
Israel’s men rallied from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, then chased Midian. 🏃

Gideon sent messengers throughout Ephraim’s hill country: ‘Come down and block Midian from the waters all the way to the Jordan at Beth Barah!’ Ephraim’s men rallied and took control of the waters up to Beth Barah and the Jordan. 📨
They captured Midian’s two commanders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at Oreb’s Rock and Zeeb at Zeeb’s winepress while chasing Midian, then brought their heads to Gideon across the Jordan. ⚔️
